scenes.title: When an answer becomes an action
scenes.viewerPurpose: An AI can give a useful answer and still make a costly mistake when it acts.
scenes.composition: A request document on the left and an unfinished action on the right, separated by a visible approval control.
addOrChange: Remove the unrelated parcel and refund story; change the action label to a proposed file edit.

cues.visualAction: A request enters; the consequential action stays pending rather than receiving a success tick.
Bring the book title into the same view while the request and pending action remain visible.

scenes.title: Who gave permission
scenes.viewerPurpose: Editing a file or using a service involves more than finding the right words.
scenes.composition: One source page beside a proposed change, with the owner’s approval between them.
addOrChange: Relabel the refund operation as a proposed change; do not imply read access authorizes edits.

cues.visualAction: Reveal the source page, then a proposed edit with its changed region highlighted.
Move the request marker toward the approval control and stop before execution.

scenes.title: When a task goes wrong
scenes.viewerPurpose: As jobs grow longer, even capable agents can lose track of the original request.
scenes.composition: A short task record with one missing step and a second person inspecting it.
addOrChange: Remove the extra handoff and nested plan panels; keep one record with a readable missing step.

cues.visualAction: Show the original request beside the incomplete record so the missed step is visible.
Invite the second reviewer to inspect the gap; show two possible next steps without selecting a winner.

scenes.title: Choosing what to trust
scenes.viewerPurpose: Builders can follow what happens when a step fails or needs to be undone.
scenes.composition: The proposed change can be reversed beside the original request and book.
addOrChange: Replace the malicious-quote illustration with a reversible file change; retain the authority boundary.

cues.visualAction: Show a changed file returning to its previous version while its record remains available.
Hold the original request beside the book with a simple Check what happens next label.

checks: Do not generate voice until all122 script and visual plans pass review.
Use only source-grounded diagrams and neutral illustrative examples; preserve uncertainty and proposal labels.
Measure audio and keep the complete film at or below120 seconds without accelerating narration.
Inspect Color, Light and Dark at desktop and phone sizes; verify captions, labels and cue timing.
Listening review and visual QA are separate from having a compiled film.
